sources.entry: FileRise - Web file manager with uploads, tagging, share links, gallery/table views, and an in-browser editor. (Demo) MIT Docker/PHP

summary.one_liner: FileRise is a self-hosted, MIT-licensed PHP web file manager with WebDAV access, per-folder ACLs, sharing links, and optional folder-level encryption at rest.
summary.what_it_does: FileRise provides a browser-based file manager with drag-and-drop chunked, resumable uploads, folder and file sharing (including upload-only file request links protected by optional passwords and expiration), and tagging with search and a Trash. Access is controlled by granular per-folder ACLs that the README says are enforced across the web UI, API, and WebDAV. It exposes a WebDAV endpoint for mounting as a network drive, an OpenAPI spec with Redoc docs, and optional ClamAV virus scanning. Optional OnlyOffice integration allows editing Office documents, and PDFs can be previewed inline. Core also supports optional folder-level encryption at rest, with the master key generated by FileRise or supplied by environment variable. It runs on Docker (recommended) or a manual PHP 8.3+ Linux web server with no database required.
use_cases: share files with external users via upload-only links
mount a web file manager as a WebDAV drive
per-folder access control for a small team
edit Office documents in the browser with OnlyOffice
encrypt sensitive folders at rest on disk
how_to_run: export PERSISTENT_TOKENS_KEY="$(openssl rand -hex 32)"  (optional; auto-generated on pristine installs)

docker run -d --name filerise -p 8080:80 -e TIMEZONE="America/New_York" -e TOTAL_UPLOAD_SIZE="10G" -e SECURE="false" -v ~/filerise/uploads:/var/www/uploads -v ~/filerise/users:/var/www/users -v ~/filerise/metadata:/var/www/metadata error311/filerise-docker:latest
Or use docker compose with the provided docker-compose.yml and run: docker compose up -d
Then open the web UI on port 8080 and create the initial admin user
Manual install: create /var/www/{uploads,users,metadata}, download the release ZIP, and point the web server DocumentRoot at the public/ folder
notable: Per-folder ACLs with view, upload, edit, rename, move, copy, delete, share and more, enforced across UI, API and WebDAV
Optional folder-level encryption at rest that automatically disables incompatible features like WebDAV, sharing and OnlyOffice
Upload-only File Request links so outsiders can submit files without seeing existing contents
Reverse proxy and subpath aware, with FR_BASE_PATH, FR_PUBLISHED_URL and trusted proxy settings
caveats: Folder encryption disables WebDAV, sharing, ZIP operations and OnlyOffice while enabled
Manual installs on shared hosting are best-effort; native Windows PHP server installs are not supported as a security boundary
Many advanced features (user groups, client portals, S3/SMB/SFTP sources, gateway shares, audit logs) are part of the paid FileRise Pro edition, not Core
